readings.commitment: The British constitution rests on its medieval and early-modern charters, in which liberty was extracted from the Crown document by document
readings.delta: Suppression of royal prerogative by accumulated grant; beneficiary is the baronage then the subject; victim set is unconstrained kingship; extractiveness of arbitrary rule bargained down in instalments

readings.commitment: The British constitution was fixed in 1688-1701: the Revolution settlement that subordinated the Crown to Parliament and statute is the operative founding
readings.delta: Suppression of Stuart absolutism and the deposed line; beneficiary is Parliament and the Protestant succession; victim set is Catholic claimants and divine-right theory; extractiveness of prerogative taxation ended

readings.commitment: The British constitution is whatever the Crown-in-Parliament enacts: the supremacy statutes that remade unions, chambers, and terms are its real text
readings.delta: Suppression of every rival constitutional veto (Lords, devolved bodies in theory); beneficiary is the Commons majority of the day; victim set is entrenchment-seekers; extractiveness revisable by bare majority

readings.commitment: The British constitution lives in its conventions: binding-but-unenforceable usages that do the daily work no statute describes
readings.delta: Suppression by expectation rather than law (breach is constitutional crisis, not illegality); beneficiary is insiders fluent in the usages; victim set is actors who mistake legal power for permitted power; extractiveness policed by scandal

readings.commitment: The British constitution has been judicialized since 1998: rights instruments, devolution, and a Supreme Court have turned political self-restraint into adjudicated limits
readings.delta: Suppression of pure political constitutionalism; beneficiary is rights-claimants and courts; victim set is parliamentary-sovereignty purists; extractiveness reviewed where it was once merely debated

readings.commitment: Magna Carta is the founding charter: the king conceded in writing that he too is under the law, and every later liberty descends from that concession
readings.delta: Suppression of arbitrary royal process (lawful judgment of peers); beneficiary is the baronage, later generalized; victim set is the Angevin fiscal machine; extractiveness of ransom-kingship bargained into legality

readings.commitment: The Petition of Right restated the medieval liberties against a modern Crown: no taxation without Parliament, no arbitrary imprisonment, no forced billeting
readings.delta: Suppression of prerogative finance and detention; beneficiary is property-holders and the imprisoned-without-cause; victim set is forced-loan kingship; extractiveness of supply re-chained to consent

readings.commitment: The Habeas Corpus Act made the ancient writ effective procedure: detention must be justified before a judge, quickly, or end
readings.delta: Suppression of indefinite executive detention; beneficiary is the detained; victim set is gaolers and ministers holding without charge; extractiveness of liberty by delay foreclosed

readings.commitment: Magna Carta was a feudal peace treaty: a defeated king's concessions to armed barons about reliefs, wardships, and scutage, annulled within months
readings.delta: Suppression confined to baronial grievances; beneficiary is the rebel baronage; victim set is royal fiscal officers; extractiveness of feudal incidents capped for one class only

readings.commitment: Magna Carta founded the common-law constitution: clauses 39 and 40 seeded due process, and its repeated reconfirmations made legality the Crown's permanent condition
readings.delta: Suppression of lawless rule generalized over centuries; beneficiary is every subject claiming process; victim set is prerogative justice; extractiveness routed through courts the Crown does not own

readings.commitment: Magna Carta's power is mythic: a document mostly repealed, misread by every generation that invoked it, whose authority is the invocation itself
readings.delta: Suppression by invocation rather than text (the myth disciplines power the clauses never reached); beneficiary is whoever wields the symbol; victim set is textual fidelity; extractiveness of the legend exceeds the parchment

readings.commitment: The Bill of Rights 1689 is the settlement's charter: suspending and dispensing powers illegal, parliamentary privilege secured, the Crown's terms of tenure rewritten
readings.delta: Suppression of prerogative legislation; beneficiary is Parliament and its members' speech; victim set is the dispensing Crown; extractiveness of taxation without consent declared illegal

readings.commitment: The Act of Settlement completed the settlement: succession by statute, judges secured during good behaviour, the Crown made a parliamentary office
readings.delta: Suppression of hereditary-right absolutism (Parliament chooses the line); beneficiary is judicial independence and the Hanoverian succession; victim set is the excluded Stuart line; extractiveness of judicial removal by displeasure ended

readings.commitment: The Toleration Act is the settlement's religious truce: dissenting worship legalized while the establishment and its tests stood, a peace bought by calibrated exclusion
readings.delta: Suppression relaxed for trinitarian dissent only; beneficiary is licensed nonconformity; victim set is Catholics and non-trinitarians still excluded; extractiveness of conformity reduced, not ended

readings.commitment: The Bill of Rights' living core is Article 9: proceedings in Parliament may not be impeached in any court, the foundation of legislative free speech
readings.delta: Suppression of judicial reach into Parliament; beneficiary is members' deliberation; victim set is litigants injured by privileged speech; extractiveness of judicial control over the chamber forbidden

readings.commitment: The Bill of Rights is a confessional instrument: its liberties were secured for Protestants, its succession clauses exclude Catholics to this day
readings.delta: Suppression organized along confessional lines; beneficiary is the Protestant establishment; victim set is Catholic subjects and heirs; extractiveness of office and crown by creed entrenched

readings.commitment: The Bill of Rights is the ancestor of modern rights charters: excessive bail, cruel punishments, jury trial — the 1791 American text quotes it nearly verbatim
readings.delta: Suppression of punitive excess in embryo; beneficiary is the accused and later constitution-writers abroad; victim set is prerogative criminal justice; extractiveness of punishment proportioned a century early

readings.commitment: The Acts of Union made the constitution's very subject by statute: England and Scotland, then Ireland, merged into one Parliament by reciprocal enactment
readings.delta: Suppression of separate parliaments; beneficiary is the metropolitan legislature and unionist commerce; victim set is the merged kingdoms' institutional autonomy; extractiveness of peripheral governance centralized

readings.commitment: The Parliament Act 1911 settled the chambers: the Lords lost money bills entirely and kept only a delaying veto, under threat of mass peer creation
readings.delta: Suppression of the hereditary veto; beneficiary is the elected Commons and its budgets; victim set is the peerage's legislative power; extractiveness of aristocratic blockage reduced to delay

readings.commitment: The Parliament Act 1949 used the 1911 procedure to shorten the Lords' delay to one year — the Act amending the terms of its own authorization
readings.delta: Suppression of the remaining delay, by bootstrap; beneficiary is the governing majority's timetable; victim set is second-chamber revision time; extractiveness of delay halved by the delayed procedure itself

readings.commitment: The Fixed-term Parliaments Act briefly statutized the election-calling power, then was repealed and the prerogative revived — supremacy demonstrated by round trip
readings.delta: Suppression of prime-ministerial timing, then un-suppression; beneficiary alternated (opposition certainty, then incumbent flexibility); victim set is whoever the cycle disadvantaged; extractiveness of electoral timing returned to the Crown's advisers

readings.commitment: The 1911 Act constitutionalized democratic supremacy: the elected chamber's will prevails and the unelected chamber may only delay
readings.delta: Suppression of unelected veto as principle; beneficiary is the franchise-holding public via the Commons; victim set is hereditary legislative power; extractiveness of class veto formally ended

readings.commitment: The 1911 Act passed only under the threat of five hundred new peers: a constitutional amendment extracted by promise of institutional flooding, not agreed
readings.delta: Suppression achieved by credible threat rather than consensus; beneficiary is the threatening government; victim set is the chamber consenting under duress; extractiveness of the settlement colored by its extraction

readings.commitment: Acts passed under the Parliament Acts are delegated, not primary, legislation: the 1911 Act created a subordinate procedure whose products courts may examine
readings.delta: Suppression of the bypass procedure's equivalence to full enactment; beneficiary is bicameral review and its defenders; victim set is single-chamber lawmaking; extractiveness of the shortcut contested in court (Jackson)

readings.commitment: Ministers answer to Parliament for their departments and resign for serious failure: the convention that makes the bureaucracy answerable through a person
readings.delta: Suppression of unaccountable administration; beneficiary is the Commons' scrutiny; victim set is ministers bearing officials' failures; extractiveness of anonymous misgovernment given a resigning face

readings.commitment: The monarch assents to every bill duly passed: a legal veto unused since 1708, alive only as the rule that it must never be used
readings.delta: Suppression of the personal Crown in legislation; beneficiary is parliamentary finality; victim set is none in practice (the power's holder most of all); extractiveness of royal legislative will reduced to ceremony

readings.commitment: Cabinet speaks with one voice: ministers defend decisions they opposed in private or leave, the convention that manufactures a single government
readings.delta: Suppression of public ministerial dissent; beneficiary is government coherence and the PM; victim set is dissenting ministers' public honesty; extractiveness of unity enforced by career

readings.commitment: The Lords do not block manifesto bills: the unelected chamber concedes mandate legislation at second reading, its self-denying terms of survival
readings.delta: Suppression of the Lords' veto over endorsed programs; beneficiary is manifesto democracy; victim set is second-chamber resistance to mandated change; extractiveness of electoral promises given passage

readings.commitment: Refusal of assent is constitutionally dead: three centuries of disuse have extinguished the power, and any refusal would simply be ignored or end the monarchy
readings.delta: Suppression complete and irreversible (desuetude as repeal); beneficiary is parliamentary certainty; victim set is reserve-power theorists; extractiveness of royal veto zero in all worlds

readings.commitment: Assent remains a true reserve power: in a genuine constitutional extremity — a bill abolishing elections — refusal is the system's last fuse
readings.delta: Suppression conditional, not extinguished (dormant against ordinary politics, live against autogolpe); beneficiary is constitutional continuity in extremis; victim set is would-be self-perpetuating majorities; extractiveness of the fuse never tested

readings.commitment: Assent is exercised only on ministerial advice: even refusal would be the government's act, the monarch a conduit with no personal discretion at all
readings.delta: Suppression of personal discretion relocated to advisers; beneficiary is the government of the day; victim set is the monarch-as-actor theory; extractiveness of the veto belongs to ministers if it exists

readings.commitment: The Human Rights Act brought the European Convention home: courts read statutes compatibly with rights and declare incompatibility they cannot fix
readings.delta: Suppression of rights-blind interpretation; beneficiary is Convention claimants in domestic courts; victim set is statutes' plain unprotective meanings; extractiveness reviewed against Convention floors

readings.commitment: Devolution rebuilt the state's interior: Scottish, Welsh, and Northern Irish legislatures with entrenched-in-practice powers Westminster may not casually recall
readings.delta: Suppression of unitary centralism in practice; beneficiary is the devolved nations' domestic agendas; victim set is uniform UK-wide policy; extractiveness of metropolitan control conditioned on convention (Sewel)

readings.commitment: The 2005 reforms made the judiciary visibly separate: the Law Lords left the legislature and a Supreme Court now faces Parliament from across the square
readings.delta: Suppression of fused judicial-legislative identity; beneficiary is separation-of-powers legibility; victim set is the old Lord Chancellor's tri-cornered office; extractiveness of judicial dependence on the chamber ended in form

readings.commitment: EU membership and its reversal bracketed the era: forty years of supremacy-sharing, then a referendum-driven exit that tested every convention it touched
readings.delta: Suppression of parliamentary sovereignty pooled then reclaimed; beneficiary contested by phase (single market, then sovereignty restorationists); victim set likewise; extractiveness of supranational rules accepted then renounced

readings.commitment: The HRA incorporated the Convention: rights are now domestic law, enforceable in any court, and the long road to Strasbourg begins at home
readings.delta: Suppression of the enforcement gap; beneficiary is claimants with domestic remedies; victim set is rights-violating public authorities; extractiveness of the trip to Strasbourg removed

readings.commitment: The HRA's genius is what it withheld: courts may declare incompatibility but never strike down — Parliament's last word survives intact
readings.delta: Suppression of judicial supremacy by design; beneficiary is the sovereignty doctrine; victim set is claimants whose declarations Parliament ignores; extractiveness of incompatible statutes continues until Parliament acts

readings.commitment: The HRA transferred power to judges: section 3 interpretation rewrites statutes in all but name, and declarations Parliament dare not ignore are strike-downs in practice
readings.delta: Suppression of legislative meaning by interpretive obligation; beneficiary is the judiciary's effective reach; victim set is enacted intention; extractiveness of political choices relocated to courtrooms

readings.commitment: Membership pooled sovereignty profitably: supremacy of EU law was Parliament's own continuing choice, revocable at will and therefore never lost
readings.delta: Suppression of national rules within chosen domains; beneficiary is market integration and treaty reciprocity; victim set is inconsistent domestic statutes while membership lasted; extractiveness of compliance traded for access

readings.commitment: Membership hollowed the constitution: courts disapplied Acts of Parliament for the first time since 1689, and 'revocable in theory' concealed subordination in fact
readings.delta: Suppression of the sovereignty doctrine's substance (Factortame); beneficiary is the supranational legal order; victim set is parliamentary finality; extractiveness of rule-making exported to institutions voters could not remove

readings.commitment: Exit proved the doctrine: the referendum and the European Union (Withdrawal) Acts demonstrated that what Parliament pooled, Parliament could take back entire
readings.delta: Suppression of the irreversibility thesis; beneficiary is the take-back-control coalition; victim set is integrationist settlement and its reliance interests; extractiveness of supranational rules ended at the price of exit costs
